analysis.title: Inside Commodities, October 27, 2026
key_insights: Russian refiners are raising diesel output after the US-Russia supply deal. Output fell to about 160,000 t/d in early October from 175,000 t/d in September and is rising toward 180,000 t/d after export quotas arrived mid-month.

Russia's domestic diesel use is about 140,000 t/d in October, leaving at least 40,000 t/d (over 1 million tons a month) for export. About 0.2-0.3 million tons of that may go to neighbouring countries. Sources expect the export ban to stay, with quotas regulating exports.

Trump said Russia would deliver over 300,000 t of diesel immediately, 500,000 t in November and 1 million t after that, plus 3 million t more depending on refinery condition. A Malta-flagged tanker with 40,000 t of Russian diesel bound for New York appeared on tracking on October 23.

Canada is moving to expand oil and LNG exports after US tariffs and the US war with Iran. PM Carney is fast-tracking the 1 million bpd Pacific Link pipeline to the west coast, which would double west-coast export capacity. It is estimated at C$35.2-43.7 billion, with construction expected to start next September.
About 90% of Canada's oil exports go to the US. Washington imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports in August after talks collapsed, and Trump said Sunday a deal was close.

Canada's Energy Minister Hodgson sees oil output rising 2-2.5 million bpd in 5-7 years and LNG exports reaching 50 mtpa by 2030 from about 14 mtpa. Commodity Context's Rory Johnston forecasts only 100,000-150,000 bpd of annual growth, citing uncertain oil prices and heavy-oil cost challenges.

China is importing bull semen again under a rule limiting imports to the best 10% of bulls in the producing country. By end-August it had received 92,573 straws worth about $700,000 from Australia and Canada, versus roughly 10 million straws a year before the curbs. Reviews take over four months per shipment.

The US supplies about 55% of the roughly $500 million of bull semen shipped globally each year and is expected to be China's dominant supplier once approved. China's beef and dairy imports run $25-30 billion a year.

EU crop monitor MARS says winter crops are hurt by dry soils in the west and southeast (rapeseed emergence in France and Germany, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia) and by excess rain in the Baltics. Baltic winter crop area is expected to decline.

MARS cut its 2026 EU grain maize yield forecast to 6.42 t/ha from 6.50 t/ha, 9% below the five-year average, and sugar beet to 67.2 t/ha from 67.4 t/ha, 12% below average. EU maize and sugar beet output is widely forecast to be the lowest in decades after the summer drought and heatwaves.

Australia is refreshing its critical minerals strategy to emphasize refining and processing, where China dominates. It is building an A$1.2 billion strategic reserve (antimony, gallium, rare earths) based on offtake agreements and forward contracts, and Europe is showing interest. The EU shortlisted tungsten, rare earths and gallium for its first joint stockpile.

Copper is holding near record highs above $14,000/t. The ICSG expects a global surplus of 104,000 t this year and 368,000 t next year. Exchange inventory is over 1.2 million t, double year-ago levels, but nearly all of it sits in the US because of tariff uncertainty.

China's copper market is very tight. SHFE inventory is 54,400 t and the Yangshan import premium is at a 13-year high of $168/t over LME. Mercuria's Snowdon called it the tightest he has seen in his career.

Aluminium premiums are split by regions because of the 50% US import tariff. Harbor Aluminum's Vazquez puts the chance of a tariff reset for Canadian metal at up to 75%, which would collapse US premiums and could nearly double European premiums to over $1,000/t above LME cash.
Nickel pricing hinges on Indonesian ore-supply policy, and cobalt on DRC export controls, which are propping up prices while stocks build inside the country.

EQT will buy Range Resources in a $13 billion all-stock deal (0.987 EQT shares per Range share, $54.91 per share, 20.6% premium). EQT fell 3.7% and Range rose 15.1% to $52.43. The combined company will produce over 9 bcfed with enterprise value over $50 billion, and close is expected in Q1 2027.

The EQT-Range deal is expected to lower EQT's unlevered free cash flow breakeven to below $2/MMBtu. The combined company expects about $20 billion of cumulative free cash flow over five years at recent prices, and EQT sees Appalachian gas demand potentially reaching 25 bcfd versus 20 bcfd before.

IEA's Birol says diesel prices are up about 200% and LNG prices up 250% from pre-war levels, and EV sales outside China are 60% above prior trend since the Iran war began. He does not expect 2027 energy markets to return to pre-war conditions.

Black Sea shipping risk is rising. At least eight cargo ships have been hit and about 34 sailors are dead or missing in three weeks, and London insurers widened the high-risk area. Constanta volumes through September were 51.55 million t, flat y/y, and grain exports were 15.8 million t, up 7%.

Russian 12.5% protein wheat FOB prices fell to $264/t (IKAR, down $3) and $270/t (Sovecon, down $5) on Black Sea peace hopes. Putin said Moscow is ready to resume trilateral talks in the first ten days of November. Sovecon's Sizov called the optimism premature.

Azov-Black Sea port shipments have been nearly at a standstill since mid-August. IKAR raised its October Russian wheat export forecast to 2.8-3.0 million t, and Rusagrotrans estimates 1.5 million t exported October 1-20.

market_movers.rationale: EQT fell 3.7% on announcing an all-stock $13 billion purchase of Range Resources. William Blair's Bert Donnes said the deal strengthens EQT's position in growing gas and power markets.
Range Resources rose 15.1% to $52.43 against a deal value of $54.91 per share, a 20.6% premium to Friday's close.

sector_views.rationale: Record US gas consumption is expected from LNG exports and AI data center power demand. EIA sees consumption rising from 91.9 bcfd in 2025 to 94.3 bcfd in 2027.
Around three-quarters of LME Seminar attendees picked copper as the top metal over the next 12 months. Demand tied to data centers is strong and supply is fragmented by policy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Holding near record highs despite a forecast global surplus, because US-held inventories leave the rest of the world short.
A small global surplus coexists with a very tight Chinese market.
A larger surplus is expected next year.

macro_indicators.reading: 91.9 bcfd in 2025 rising to 94.3 bcfd in 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports demand for gas producers, driven by LNG exports and power generation.

macro_indicators.reading: about 160,000 t/d in first half of October, rising toward 180,000 t/d
macro_indicators.interpretation: Output is recovering after export quotas were granted under the US deal.
High fuel prices are pushing consumers toward alternatives such as EVs, solar and coal.
Reflects the Hormuz disruption and supports LNG supply diversification.
Down $3 w/w on Black Sea peace hopes.

risk_factors: US copper tariff decision could unwind the US stockpile and shift the global balance
Black Sea ship attacks and higher insurance premiums threaten grain and fuel flows
Premature Black Sea peace optimism (Sovecon) could reverse wheat price declines
Russian diesel exports depend on refinery condition and the government keeping quota controls
Canadian output targets may be too ambitious given price uncertainty and heavy-oil costs
EU drought and excess rain cut crop yields and could reduce rapeseed area
Policy-driven supply constraints in nickel (Indonesia) and cobalt (DRC)
vol_and_positioning: LME Seminar poll: about three-quarters picked copper as top performer over 12 months, falling to about half once tin was included.
Copper stocks are concentrated in the US (over 1.2 million t exchange inventory, double a year ago) while SHFE stocks are just 54,400 t.
geopolitical: US-Russia diesel supply deal with temporary US sanctions relief on Russian fuel
US war with Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz after the February 28 offensive
US-Canada trade dispute, including 50% US tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports
Escalating attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea off Romania and Bulgaria
Putin ready to resume trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington in the first ten days of November
Possible US tariff decisions on copper imports and a possible tariff reset for Canadian aluminium
Indonesian ore policy affecting nickel and DRC export controls affecting cobalt

tension_points.bull_case: Demand tied to data centers and policy-fragmented supply make copper the top pick for the next 12 months, with China's market the tightest Mercuria has seen and the Yangshan premium at a 13-year high.
tension_points.bear_case: The ICSG expects a global surplus of 104,000 t this year and 368,000 t next, and exchange inventory of over 1.2 million t is double year-ago levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US decision on copper import tariffs, which would release the metal stockpiled in the US.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy Minister Hodgson sees production rising 2-2.5 million bpd over 5-7 years, backed by the Pacific Link pipeline and west coast access to Asia.
tension_points.bear_case: Commodity Context's Johnston forecasts only 100,000-150,000 bpd of growth a year because producers hesitate to invest amid price uncertainty, and heavy crude carries a price discount.

tension_points.theme: Black Sea peace and wheat prices
tension_points.bull_case: Putin said Moscow is ready to resume trilateral talks in the first ten days of November, and wheat export prices have fallen on peace hopes.
tension_points.bear_case: Sovecon's Sizov believes the optimism is premature, and attacks on vessels continue with Azov-Black Sea port shipments nearly at a standstill since mid-August.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Talks failing to resume in the first ten days of November.

theme_stances.key_argument: Copper demand is strong and supply is fragmented by government policy, leaving the US oversupplied and the rest of the world short.
theme_stances.evidence: demand is "everything, everywhere all at once," but supply is fragmented by government policy

theme_stances.evidence: We believe the optimism is premature

theme_stances.key_argument: Canada is seeking to export more oil and LNG to Asia through new west-coast pipeline capacity to reduce dependence on the US.
theme_stances.evidence: we just intend to trade a lot more with other people
